title.en: EU member states: membership and the euro

description.en: The 27 member states of the European Union as of October 2026: the year each became a member (27 cards) and, for the 21 that use the euro, the year each joined the euro area (21 cards). Front: the country and the question, e.g. “Sweden: EU member since which year?” or “Finland: euro area member since which year?”; back: the year, with the full date in a note. The six founders count from 1958, when the Treaties of Rome came into force (some sources give 1957, the year they were signed); the euro year is when the country joined the euro area, which for the first eleven was 1999, when the euro was introduced for non-cash payments (notes and coins came in 2002). Taken from the EU's country profiles on european-union.europa.eu and Wikidata, and checked against the European Central Bank.
description.sv: EU:s 27 medlemsländer i oktober 2026: året då varje land blev medlem (27 kort) och, för de 21 som har euron, året då landet gick med i euroområdet (21 kort). Framsida: landet och frågan, t.ex. ”Sverige: EU-medlem sedan vilket år?” eller ”Finland: medlem i euroområdet sedan vilket år?”; baksida: året, med det fullständiga datumet i en anteckning. De sex grundarländerna räknas från 1958, då Romfördragen trädde i kraft (vissa källor anger 1957, då de undertecknades); euroåret är året då landet gick med i euroområdet, vilket för de första elva var 1999, då euron infördes för kontantlösa betalningar (sedlar och mynt kom 2002). Uppgifterna är hämtade från EU:s landsfakta på european-union.europa.eu och Wikidata och kontrollerade mot Europeiska centralbanken.

method: Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts). Quality-control round 0 records the authoring agent's own source and machine checks; reviews by independent AI reviewers are recorded as further rounds when they have been made. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.

The set of member states: the EU's own list of countries (query 6, european-union.europa.eu/principles-countries-history/eu-countries_en, fetched on 2026-10-04) shows "Pages (27)" and the year filter "Countries by year of entry 1958 1973 1981 1986 1995 2004 2007 2013". Wikidata gave the same 27 (query 2: items with a P463 "member of" statement for the European Union, Q458, of any rank, with the P580/P582 qualifiers; the United Kingdom, Q145, is the one item with an end time, 2020-01-31). A first Wikidata query (query 1) that also required P31 sovereign state (Q3624078) returned only 25 of them, because the Netherlands (Q55) and Denmark (Q35) are modelled as constituent countries of their kingdoms; the class filter was dropped.

Dates: fetch_profiles.py (query 5, whose full source is recorded there) downloaded the English and Swedish country profile of each of the 27 countries (…/eu-countries/<country>_en and …_sv) and extracted the overview, which gives "EU Member State: since <date>" and, for euro countries, "Euro area: member since <date>" (in Swedish "EU-medlem: Sedan den …" and "Euroområdet: Medlem sedan den …"). The year on each back is the year of these dates; the full date is in the back note. The English and Swedish pages agree on every date. Countries whose profile names another currency (Czechia, Denmark, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden) have no euro card.

Conventions: for the six founders the profiles give 1 January 1958, the day the Treaties of Rome (signed 25 March 1957) came into force and the EEC and Euratom came into being (europa.eu history page 1945-59, query 8; EUR-Lex summary of the EEC Treaty, query 10). Other sources use 1957 (the ECB) or record the signing date (Wikidata), so the convention is stated in the description and in each founder's back note. For the euro, the year is when the country joined the euro area: the profiles give 1 January 1999 for the first eleven, when the euro was introduced for non-cash transactions (europa.eu history page 1990-99, query 8), and 1 January 2001 for Greece; notes and coins came on 1 January 2002 (europa.eu history page 2000-09, query 13, entry "1 January 2002 – Euro notes and coins launch in 12 countries"), which the back notes of those twelve cards say. From Slovenia (2007) on, the profiles, the ECB and Wikidata give one date.

Names: the English names are the profiles' ("Czechia" rather than Wikidata's English label "Czech Republic", which has "Czechia" as an alias; "Netherlands"). The Swedish names are the Wikidata Swedish labels (query 4), each identical to the name the Swedish profile uses in its title and text (Österrike, Belgien, Tjeckien, Nederländerna …). The Swedish card wording follows the Swedish profiles ("EU-medlem sedan", "Medlem sedan den", "euroområdet"); month names are lower-case in the Swedish notes.

Cross-check against the European Central Bank: the ECB's page "Our money" (query 7; the old address …/map.en.html redirects to …/index.en.html) has a table of the EU members with "Joined the EU" and "Adopted the euro" ("1999 (cash since 2002)", Greece "2001 (cash since 2002)", Bulgaria "2026"), and lists Czech Republic, Denmark, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Sweden as not using the euro. Every card agrees with it except the founders' year (ECB 1957), which follows the stated convention. Bulgaria's euro date, the most recent change, was checked a third time against the Commission's page "Bulgaria and the euro" (query 12).

Cross-check against Wikidata (query 2 and query 3): the P580 start time of each later member's P463 Q458 statement is the profiles' date (1973-01-01 … 2013-07-01). Wikidata gives 1957-03-25 for Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands and 1958-01-01 for Germany. Wikidata's euro P38 statements (Q4916, preferred rank) have start times equal to the profiles' dates except Germany, Italy and Greece, where they are 2002-01-01, the date the notes and coins replaced the national currency. These differences are recorded in each card's evidence and in quality control; the cards follow the EU's own dates.

Notes were written in the compiler's own words from the dates above. make_dossier.py (query 14, its key steps recorded there) wrote the cards from the saved files (profiles.json, the Wikidata CSV results of queries 2–4 and the ECB page): it stripped the HTML tags from each page (scripts and styles removed, every tag replaced by a space, entities unescaped, runs of whitespace collapsed to one space), removed the space this leaves before a colon (regular expression \s+: replaced by :), and took each quoted date as the exact match of the patterns "EU Member State: since (\d+) (\w+) (\d{4})", "EU-medlem: Sedan den (\d+) (\w+) (\d{4})", "Euro area: member since (\d+) (\w+) (\d{4})" and "Euroområdet: Medlem sedan den (\d+) (\w+) (\d{4})" in the profile overviews, and each ECB quote as the country's row in the ECB table. The quotes from the history pages and EUR-Lex were copied from the page text by hand, with the space the tag stripping left before a comma or full stop removed.

Machine checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: for every card the English (for Czechia the alias "Czechia") and Swedish label of the country; for every membership card P463 = Q458, except Romania, whose Q458 statement is not a truthy value because another of its P463 statements has preferred rank; for every euro card P38 = Q4916. The builder can check only direct (truthy) values, not the P580 qualifiers, so the years were compared with Wikidata through queries 2 and 3 as described above.
selection: All 27 member states of the European Union on 2026-10-04, as the EU's own list shows them, with one card each for the year of membership, and the 21 of them that use the euro, with one card each for the year they joined the euro area. Not included: the United Kingdom, a member from 1973 until it left on 31 January 2020; the six members that do not use the euro (Czechia, Denmark, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden) have no euro card; countries that use the euro without being EU members (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City, Montenegro, Kosovo) and candidate countries. The membership year is the year in the EU's country profiles: for the founders 1958, when the Treaties of Rome came into force, not 1952 (the European Coal and Steel Community) or 1957 (the signing) — the European Union itself was created by the Maastricht Treaty on 1 November 1993, and membership is counted, as the EU counts it, from the Communities that became the EU. Former territories and changes of borders (such as German reunification in 1990) are not covered. The euro year is the year of joining the euro area, not of the cash changeover. Facts that could change (new members, new euro countries) are as of October 2026.
licensing: The deck is CC BY 4.0 because its main content source, the EU's website european-union.europa.eu (the country profiles and the three history pages for 1945-59, 1990-99 and 2000-09, each recorded as its own source), is CC BY 4.0 under the Commission's reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU); the deck attributes it in its metadata (prov:wasDerivedFrom, with title, creator and licence) and in this report, and the cards are the compiler's own wording of the dates, which is a change from the source and is stated as such here. The other content source, Wikidata, is CC0. The verification sources contributed no text or selection: the ECB's website is copyright of the ECB with reuse allowed on its own conditions (treated as all rights reserved, verification only), and the EUR-Lex summary and the Commission's page on Bulgaria are CC BY 4.0 but only confirmed facts the content sources gave. The selection is the complete set of current EU members and of the euro-area members, not a choice taken from anyone's list. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence remain under their sources' licences and are given only to make the checks verifiable.

5. fetch_profiles.py, run as "python3 fetch_profiles.py": the 54 country profiles, each fetched with the User-Agent "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"; the overview (from "Capital"/"Huvudstad" to "Figures"/"Fakta") extracted from the text with the HTML tags stripped and saved as profiles.json. The query field is the script's full source.
queries.query:
"""Fetch the 27 EU country profiles (en and sv) from european-union.europa.eu and extract the overview."""
import html, json, re, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(__file__).parent
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
SLUGS = ["austria", "belgium", "bulgaria", "croatia", "cyprus", "czechia", "denmark", "estonia", "finland",
         "france", "germany", "greece", "hungary", "ireland", "italy", "latvia", "lithuania", "luxembourg",
         "malta", "netherlands", "poland", "portugal", "romania", "slovakia", "slovenia", "spain", "sweden"]
out = {}
for slug in SLUGS:
    for lang in ("en", "sv"):
        url = f"https://european-union.europa.eu/principles-countries-history/eu-countries/{slug}_{lang}"
        print(url)
        f = D / "profiles" / f"{slug}_{lang}.html"
        f.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        if not f.exists():
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
            f.write_bytes(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60).read())
            time.sleep(0.5)
        t = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        t = re.sub(r"<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>", "", t, flags=re.S)
        t = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", t))
        t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t)
        title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.S)
        i = t.find("Capital") if lang == "en" else t.find("Huvudstad")
        j = t.find("Figures") if lang == "en" else t.find("Fakta")
        if j < 0 or j < i:
            j = i + 600
        out[f"{slug}_{lang}"] = {"url": url, "title": title.group(1).strip() if title else None, "overview": t[i:j].strip()}
(D / "profiles.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
for k, v in out.items():
    print(k, "|", v["title"], "|", v["overview"])

def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+:", ":", s).strip()

# ECB table rows.
t = open(D / "ecb_map.html", encoding="utf-8").read()

    m = re.search(re.escape(ename) + r" (\d{4})(?: (\d{4}(?: \(cash since 2002\))?))?(?= [A-Z]|$)", table)

for slug, qid, en, ename in STATES:

    m = re.search(r"EU Member State: since (\d+) (\w+) (\d{4})", ov_en)       # membership card, en quote

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every date against the EU's English and Swedish country profiles, Wikidata and the ECB; the founders' convention against the EU history page and EUR-Lex; Bulgaria's euro date also against the Commission; the names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish profiles.
rounds.scope: All 48 cards (27 membership, 21 euro), the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: The EU's profiles (English and Swedish), the ECB and Wikidata agree on the membership year of the 21 later members and on the euro year of 18 of the 21 euro countries. The differences are conventions, not errors: the founders' year (EU profiles 1958, ECB 1957, Wikidata 1957 for five and 1958 for Germany) and the euro year of Germany, Italy and Greece in Wikidata (2002, the cash changeover). The cards follow the EU's own dates and state the conventions. Builder checks cover the English and Swedish country names of every card, P463 Q458 on 26 of 27 membership cards and P38 Q4916 on all euro cards; no check was dropped because Wikidata disagreed, but the qualifier years cannot be machine-checked by the builder.

findings.issue: Founders' year differs by source: the EU's profiles say "since 1 January 1958" (Treaties of Rome in force), the ECB "EU founding member in 1957", Wikidata P580 1957-03-25 for Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands and 1958-01-01 for Germany; 1952 (ECSC) is a third possible convention. A card without a stated convention would have no single right answer.
findings.resolution: All six founder cards (belgium-eu, france-eu, germany-eu, italy-eu, luxembourg-eu, netherlands-eu) give 1958, the EU's own date, confirmed by the EU history page and the EUR-Lex summary (applied from 1 January 1958). The description and each founder's back note state the convention and mention 1957.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P38 euro statement for Germany starts 2002-01-01 (the Deutsche Mark ends 2001-12-31); the EU profile and the ECB give 1999 for the euro area (cash since 2002). The same for Italy (2002-01-01) and Greece (2002-01-01, the EU and ECB give 2001).
